title: Regional multi-zone dedicated fleet: placement, failover & data residency policy
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Define product and policy requirements for regional and multi-zone Dedicated fleets. Deliver a placement policy surface, failover behaviors, and hard data-residency controls that let customers: (1) guarantee throughput and latency within a single region; (2) opt into multi-zone/active-passive fleets for higher availability; (3) enforce that request data, cached prefixes, and logs never leave selected geographic boundaries. This ticket captures PM requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout approach, and cross-functional dependencies (runtime, control plane, legal, pricing).
acceptance_criteria: Placement policy enum exposed in Dedicated fleet config: single_region, multi_zone_within_region, multi_region_active_passive, multi_region_active_active (beta)
Failover policy knobs: immediate-failover, graceful-evacuate, regional-fallback with configurable retry window
Data residency tag enforced in control plane and routing: region constraint prevents routing to capacity outside the allowed regions
Throughput guarantees documented per-fleet: baseline throughput, 99th percentile latency SLO, and burst capacity semantics
Automated tests that validate placement and data residency on staging: synthetic traffic and negative tests for cross-region routing
Console UX for fleet creation shows residency, estimated unit cost delta, and expected failover behavior
Runtime changes include per-fleet capacity reservation and metrics emitted for regional failover events
Legal signoff obtained for residency and audit log retention options
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chosen default placement model: single_region (strong residency) + optional multi_zone_within_region for AZ-level HA
2026-03-04: Deferred multi_region_active_active to beta - complexity & cost trade-offs identified; will ship active-passive first
2026-03-06: Agreed failover default: graceful-evacuate with 30s retry window, customers can set immediate-failover for lower latency needs
2026-03-09: Data residency enforcement will be implemented at control-plane routing + tag checks in serving runtime; encrypted KV cache keys will include territory tag

rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): expose single_region + multi_zone_within_region; control-plane + runtime changes; internal smoke tests
Phase 2 (closed beta): invite 3 enterprise customers with residency requirements; add console UI and SLA docs; measure failover metrics
Phase 3 (general availability): enforce residency in control plane; billing & pricing updates published; legal/compliance docs released
Post-GA: alpha for multi_region_active_passive and cost-optimization guidance for cross-region fleets
risks: Cross-region active-active increases egress costs and complicates KV cache consistency
Misconfiguration could silently route customer traffic outside allowed boundaries if control-plane checks are incomplete
Throughput guarantees in multi-zone setups may be weaker due to inter-AZ variability
Legal/regulatory edge-cases for customers with 'data never leaves country' requirements may require on-premise/private deployment instead
notes: Legal (2026-03-05): need explicit audit trail for residency decisions and export controls; prepare a short doc for compliance teams
